skill.name: onboarding-helper
skill.description: Generate structured onboarding guides, setup checklists, learning paths, and team process documentation for new developers.
skill.summary: Create developer onboarding documentation that covers setup, architecture, first tasks, team workflows, and support resources.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily an onboarding documentation template, and most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, example commands, placeholder environment variables, and resource links. Real risks remain where the guide recommends remote script execution through a shell and force-killing processes during troubleshooting.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands are piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell and bash command-substitution examples with package-manager instructions, checksum verification, or links to official installation pages.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting suggests force-killing processes with xargs kill -9.
remediation.suggestion: Use safer guidance that identifies the process first and asks the user to terminate only the confirmed development server process.

remediation.issue: Credential setup examples mention shared vaults and secret variable names.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders, but add guidance to use least-privilege development credentials and never paste secrets into generated documentation or chat transcripts.

static_findings.snippet: - **Port 3000 in use**: Kill the process with `lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9`
- **Database connection failed**: Check Docker is running with `docker ps`
- **Module not found**: Delete `node_modules` and run `npm install` again
**Finding Tasks**: Check Jira board for issues labeled `good-first-issue`.
- **Port 3000 in use**: Kill the process with `lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9`
Check 1Password vault "Development Secrets" or ask in #engineering.

content.value_statement: New developers often lose time finding setup steps, architecture context, and team practices. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce clear onboarding guides with checklists, milestones, and support resources.
actual_capabilities: Creates day-one, week-one, and month-one onboarding plans for developers.
Drafts environment setup guides with prerequisites, commands, and verification steps.
Documents architecture, technology stack, domain concepts, and common workflows.
Builds first-task tutorials, learning paths, FAQs, and troubleshooting sections.
Organizes team processes such as code review, branching, communication, and support contacts.
limitations: It depends on accurate project input and may produce generic examples without repository details.
It does not verify commands, links, or credentials unless asked to inspect the project.
It may include sensitive process details if the user supplies them without redaction.
It cannot replace human review from engineering, security, and people teams.

use_cases.title: Prepare a new engineer guide
use_cases.description: Create a structured onboarding document that explains setup, architecture, first tasks, and team contacts.

use_cases.title: Standardize project setup
use_cases.description: Turn scattered setup notes into a clear checklist with prerequisites, commands, validation steps, and troubleshooting tips.

use_cases.title: Build a learning path
use_cases.description: Create progressive milestones and exercises that help contributors understand the codebase and delivery process.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic onboarding guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a developer onboarding guide for this project. Include day-one setup, key tools, first task ideas, and who to ask for help.

prompt_templates.title: Document environment setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an environment setup guide for a new developer. Include prerequisites, installation steps, configuration placeholders, verification checks, and common troubleshooting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a 30-day onboarding path
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 30-day onboarding plan for a new backend engineer. Include learning goals, codebase areas, starter tasks, review checkpoints, and expected outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and improve onboarding materials
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our current onboarding notes and propose a complete improved structure. Identify missing setup steps, unclear ownership, risky credential guidance, and gaps in first-week learning.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding docs for a React and Node.js product team.
output: A welcome section with project goals and team context.
A setup checklist for tools, repository access, local services, and validation.
A first-week plan with architecture reading, starter tasks, and buddy check-ins.

output_examples.input: Help a new developer make their first contribution.
output: A guided first-task tutorial with branch creation, code changes, tests, review steps, and merge expectations.
A list of support channels and escalation paths for common blockers.

output_examples.input: Improve our setup guide for security.
output: A revised setup section that uses placeholders for secrets.
A warning to use approved credential storage and avoid pasting secrets into documentation.
Safer alternatives for remote installer and process termination commands.

best_practices: Provide project-specific facts, verified commands, and current team processes before generating the guide.
Review all credential, access, and deployment sections before sharing onboarding materials.
Keep the guide task-oriented with clear checkpoints for day one, week one, and month one.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated credentials, internal URLs, or production access details without review.
Do not rely on generic templates when the project has custom setup or compliance needs.
Do not include destructive commands unless they are clearly explained and safer alternatives are considered.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Engineering managers, tech leads, and developer experience teams can use it to draft onboarding materials for new developers.

faq.question: Does it inspect my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. It creates guidance from the context you provide unless you ask the agent to inspect files with available tools.

faq.question: Can it create role-specific onboarding plans?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the role, team, stack, and expected responsibilities so the output matches the new developer needs.

faq.question: Can it include setup commands?
faq.answer: Yes, but commands should be verified by a project maintainer before the guide is published or shared.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use placeholders and approved credential-management instructions. Never include real secrets in prompts or generated documentation.

faq.question: Is the output ready to publish?
faq.answer: It is a strong draft. Review it for accuracy, security, internal policy, and current ownership before publishing.
